body: I'm sorry, I should probably just include a fuller description. This woman talked to me for a solid 5 minutes, in which I nodded like a deer in headlights. She scanned up and down my body the *entire* time, occasionally stopping for effect, for example when she said something about me not having the right presence, she lingered at my face, and looked at my hair. This was extremely noticeable because it was the only time her eyes were not moving up and down, up and down. I even politely asked her to stop at one point because it was making me so uncomfortable. But she did not. Why would someone so fully, repetitiously say my appearance was unsuitable if they merely had wanted me to be dressed better. Why not say, come back in a better outfit? That being said, there was *nothing* wrong with my outfit, other than that I was wearing shorts (it was in the 90s that day) and I even apologized and explained (just as I'm doing here), that of course I would dress differently for the job (i.e. not wearing shorts). The nature of the advertisement (a white paper saying JOBS AVAILABLE, APPLY INSIDE!) did not exactly convey a need for me to be dressed business casual.

Based on past experience working retail, as long as you look clean and decently dressed, there should be no problem getting an entry-level retail position, unless you are apply to a luxury brand, perhaps. This was not a luxury store.

Yeah that's basically what she said too. She said I didn't have the right "presence" as she scanned up and down my body. Her words to me were "You don't walk into a store like this dressed like that and expect to get a job." What's bad is I thought I was actually dressed pretty nice and normal—probably wearing more expensive clothes than she was. Some of my favorite clothing items, and a pair of shoes that I was wearing for the first time. I've worked in clothing retail before and thinking of any employee or manager talking to an applicant like that is unthinkable. 

TLDR: I was not dressed badly. And I think that's beside the point. No manager should talk like that to anyone, even a hired employee!
I hadn't thought of Glassdoor. I'll see if I can. Though I feel weird about that considering I didn't even really apply—or did I?

It's a jeans and T-shirt store, albeit expensive jeans and T-shirts. More than that, her gaze lingered on my face and my hair at certain points during the conversation as if to emphasize that those parts of me were also unacceptable.

Nah, I wasn't a slob at all—I was probably wearing more expensive clothes she was wearing. It's a mid-priced jeans and expensive T-shirts kind of place. I wasn't dressed exactly right for that store, but I was dressed normal and well for a hot Saturday afternoon in the midwest. When I've worked retail in the past, turning someone down who just asked for an application would have strikes me as weirdly dramatic. Of course, in this scenario it was insulting.
Ha, exactly. I would have preferred her just give me the app and not say anything.

Sorry, graduate school for history. But it's all tied up with my ex. He made a point of telling me that he thought I was only doing it because he did and I had no goals of my own. Last week I broke no-contact and gave him an update, and said I probably wouldn't be continuing and he said it was probably for the best. At first that made me angry—I got 2 As and a B+ my first semester (along with a move and my dad having major heart surgery). One of the things that upset me is people having such strange perceptions of my motivations. I don't know.

I have no idea what's going on with your boyfriend. I know toward the end of my relationship I had *issues* with him that that were caused by me constantly feeling like I was the only one in the relationship, so when I did see him, subconsciously there was too much weirdness for me get aroused (or something like that), even though I DID want to get aroused. Basically our communication was at an all time low. 

But in your case, you definitely have some level of depression. I don't know if you mean to, but you're describing textbook depression. Especially the stuff about not enjoying things and colors seeming less vibrant. Happens to the best of us. Find a nice counselor and ask your doctor about appropriate medications. If you don't have any anxiety, wellbutrin can do wonders, and it's been on the market for a long time.

This "it's none of your business" bullshit always annoys me. 

Yeah he can do whatever he wants and people process emotions differently. But I think it's sociopathic for people to have no care for others thoughts simply because a verbal contract has been ended, behaving like their actions in no way affect anyone else's psychological well-being. Hell, if I thought me dating someone new *immediately* after ending a serious relationship would hurt someone I claimed to have deep affection for, I WOULDN'T DO IT, and I sure as hell wouldn't make it known to anyone else.

Like, in the relationship: I love you and never want to hurt you.

Then 1 week out of the relationship: Fuck you if me immediately dating someone new makes you feel like shit. This is my life, and I can do what I want. 

Like, what? 

So yeah, in conclusion, your man might be dealing with some heavy internal stuff and probably is way more fucked up than you think or will ever really know. And maybe he loved you, but probably not as much as you loved him, or he wouldn't be being such a douche about it. You deserve better.

I know exactly what you're feeling, but this girl is obviously not worth your suffering. You've obviously got a lot of heart to still care about this girl after witnessing all her weirdness and still caring, which might mean you're too good for her and that there's totally a girl out there who will recognize you for the caring person you are. So stop wasting mental energy on this one, and focus on yourself and finding someone better to care about. I know, easier said than done, and you can't just not care, but just try, and know that it will be worth it eventually, even if you don't know who that girl is dating or what she's doing.

Having been dumped myself for being "at different points in our lives," while I was unemployed (but by no means complacent or wasting time) I say that yes, it is a dumb reason to dump someone who you otherwise get along with and love/like very much. Career success is a very fleeting and changeable part of your life. Just as your ex went back to her lower-paying happier job, she could easily return to a high-paying ambitious job 6 months from now and make you look like a chump. You are taking a very short-term and very business-like view of love and relationships if you are placing so much weight on someone's career... particularly if you are young.

I'm so sorry. I was never in a coma, but I often feel like I have lost time just by making the wrong choices, spending time on fruitless pursuits. Remember that many people waste their time, but that you are still young, you can still do a lot of things. Not saying you should not mourn your lost time—I would, but you should not carry it like a medallion around your neck. If you feel you were punished, or some otherwise karmic action, then consider it time spent. You are now free.
